name: Mexico
summary: Two network operators, Telcel (América Móvil, preponderant) and AT&T México, plus Movistar (Telefónica), which runs on AT&T's radio network and has been returning spectrum, and the state-backed wholesale 700 MHz network Altán Redes. The IFT was replaced by the Comisión Reguladora de Telecomunicaciones (CRT) in October 2025; no mobile spectrum auction has been completed since IFT-10 (2021).

operators.name: Telcel
operators.legal: Radiomóvil Dipsa, S.A. de C.V. (América Móvil)
operators.notes: Declared preponderant economic agent (AEP) in telecoms since 2014.

operators.name: AT&T México
operators.legal: AT&T Comunicaciones Digitales, S. de R.L. de C.V.
operators.notes: Formed 2015 from Iusacell/Unefon and Nextel México. Hosts Movistar's traffic under the 2019 AT&T–Telefónica access agreement.

operators.name: Movistar
operators.notes: Moved its customers onto AT&T's radio network (2019 agreement) and has been returning spectrum; by Dec 2020 IFT counted only PCS and a sliver of 850 MHz for it. Holdings after 2021 not verified.

operators.name: Altán Redes
operators.legal: Altán Redes, S.A.P.I. de C.V. (Red Compartida)
operators.notes: Wholesale-only national shared network on 700 MHz (concession from 2017). Went through concurso mercantil from 2021; the federal government became majority owner. Ownership details after 2023 not verified.

bands.label: 600 MHz (n71)
bands.note: Unassigned: IFT counted 2×35 MHz available (Dec 2020). The IFT-12 auction that would have offered it was cancelled in Jan 2025; the CRT's 2026 annual band programme again lists 600 MHz for 5G access.

bands.label: 700 MHz APT (B28)
bands.note: Whole APT FDD allocation (2×45 MHz) is held nationally by the wholesale Red Compartida; IFT counts Altán with 90 MHz in the 700 MHz band.

blocks.notes: National concession for the Red Compartida (2017); IFT Tabla 9: 90 MHz.

bands.label: 800 MHz (EU B20)
bands.note: EU 800 MHz plan not used; 814–824/859–869 MHz (B26 extension) is shown under 850.

bands.label: 850 MHz cellular (B5)
bands.note: Licensed in nine cellular regions (Regiones Celulares 1–9): Telcel holds the incumbent B-side in all regions, AT&T the other side (ex-Iusacell/Unefon/Telefónica). IFT's Dec 2020 table counts only 39.38 MHz (both directions) of the 50 MHz band as concessioned, with none listed as available.

bands.label: AWS (1710–1780/2110–2180)
bands.note: Mostly national concessions (Licitación 21, 2010; IFT-3, 2016: AT&T 1 national + regional A blocks, Telcel 1 national + regional A blocks plus G and J blocks). IFT Dec 2020: Telcel 80 MHz, AT&T 50 MHz (both directions). 1755–1760/2155–2160 was offered in IFT-10 and not sold.

bands.note: Licensed by region (Licitación 20, 2010, and earlier). IFT Dec 2020 (both directions): Telefónica 43.31, AT&T 32.10, Telcel 28.40 MHz; G block (1910–1915/1990–1995) offered in IFT-10 and not sold. IFT counts 113.81 of 130 MHz.

bands.label: 1900/2000 MHz unpaired TDD
bands.note: No unpaired 1.9/2 GHz TDD assignments; 2 GHz MSS/ATC handled in separate tenders (IFT-9, IFT-13).

bands.label: 2100 MHz (B1)
bands.note: B1 not used: 2110–2170 MHz is AWS downlink and 1920–1980 MHz overlaps PCS.

bands.label: 2300 MHz (B40)
bands.note: No mobile assignment. The CRT consulted (Jun–Jul 2026) on a first 'redes inteligentes' tender of up to 40 MHz in the upper 2.3 GHz band for private industrial networks.

bands.label: 2.5 GHz FDD (B7)
bands.note: IFT-7 (2018) sold F1–F4 (2530–2570/2650–2690, 2×10 each): F1–F2 to AT&T, F3–F4 to Telefónica (Pegaso). IFT's Dec 2020 table gives AT&T 80 MHz and Telefónica 0 in 2.5 GHz, implying F3–F4 passed to AT&T (inferred). 2500–2530/2620–2650 is Telcel's (existing holdings plus block C1 won in IFT-10, 2021); TV Zac holds it in part of Zacatecas (0.65 MHz pop-weighted).

blocks.notes: IFT: 51.05 MHz pop-weighted (Dec 2020) + IFT-10 block C1 (8.3 MHz). Not held in part of Zacatecas (TV Zac).
IFT-7 blocks F3–F4, won by Pegaso PCS (Telefónica); counted for AT&T by IFT in Dec 2020 (transfer inferred)

bands.label: 2.5 GHz TDD (B41/n41)
bands.note: IFT-7 (2018): T1 2575–2595 and T2 2595–2615 MHz (20 MHz each) both won by AT&T; 2570–2575 and 2615–2620 are guard bands.

bands.label: 3.3–3.6 GHz (n77/n78)
bands.note: IFT's Dec 2020 mobile-spectrum table counted only the 3.3 GHz band (3300–3400 MHz) with 50 MHz available and unassigned; 3.4–3.6 GHz legacy fixed-wireless concessions were not counted. Telcel and AT&T are reported to run 5G NR in 3.5 GHz, but their assignments could not be verified from regulator documents.

bands.label: 4.4–5.0 GHz (n79)
bands.note: Not identified for IMT in Mexico.

bands.label: 26 GHz (n258)
bands.note: No mmWave IMT assignments; not in the CRT 2026 annual band programme.

bands.label: 37–43.5 GHz (n259/n260)
bands.note: No IMT assignments; the CRT 2026 annual programme lists 37 GHz for fixed wireless service.

bands.label: 47 GHz (n262)
bands.note: No IMT assignments or plans.

notes: Regulator: the IFT (autonomous regulator since 2013) was dissolved under the Dec 2024 constitutional reform and the Ley en Materia de Telecomunicaciones y Radiodifusión (DOF 16 Jul 2025); the Comisión Reguladora de Telecomunicaciones (CRT, attached to the Agencia de Transformación Digital y Telecomunicaciones) took over on 17 Oct 2025. The IFT website is now a read-only archive.

The IFT-12 auction (600 MHz, 800 MHz, L-band, 2.5 GHz etc.) was cancelled on 16 Jan 2025 at the ATDT's request. As of Sep 2026 the CRT has consulted on a 2.3 GHz private-network tender and a rural-coverage spectrum tender (consultation 24 Sep–21 Oct 2026), but no mobile auction has been held.

Holdings are the IFT's own population-weighted national averages as of the IFT-10 bases (Dec 2020, 'Tabla 9', figures given both directions — halved here to per-direction), updated with the IFT-10 results (Oct 2021). Licences for 850 MHz, 800 MHz and PCS are regional (nine cellular regions or smaller ABS areas); AWS and 2.5 GHz are essentially national.
IFT Tabla 9 total (both directions): Telcel 180.96 MHz, AT&T 182.23, Altán 90, Telefónica 44.25, TV Zac 0.65; plus 45.1 MHz offered in IFT-10 and 211 MHz available (600 MHz, L-band, 3.3 GHz).
missing: Changes after Oct 2021 are not reflected except where noted: in particular Telefónica/Movistar's spectrum returns after Dec 2020 (its PCS and 850 MHz holdings may now be zero) and any transfers between AT&T and Telcel could not be verified — the IFT/CRT concession registry and statistics portal (bit.ift.org.mx) were not usable.
2.5 GHz FDD: transfer of IFT-7 blocks F3–F4 from Telefónica to AT&T is inferred from IFT's Dec 2020 holdings table, not from a transfer resolution.
3.3–3.6 GHz: Telcel/AT&T 5G assignments (reported 2021–2024) not verified; entry left as 'unknown'.
Regional detail (which region each 850/PCS block belongs to) not compiled; only IFT's national pop-weighted figures are used.
Altán Redes ownership/restructuring after 2023 and Telefónica México's corporate status in 2026 not verified.
